title: When the Thorn Turns Again
premise: Dominic Thackeray, the last swordspeaker sworn to a guild that trades in impossible things, has spent fifteen years hiding her gift behind ledgers and silence. When a child named Wren arrives speaking the dead tongue of Aldermere—a country erased from every map—Dominic realizes the usurper's armies are hunting the language itself, because whoever speaks it can reopen the door out of Aldermere and claim what lies beyond. Gathering a found family of guild misfits, Dominic must relearn the oath she forswore, find the door hidden in the free cities' oldest foundations, and choose whether to seal Aldermere away forever or let its exiles return. In the end she breaks her own oath to speak the door open, sacrifices her gift to hold it against the usurper, and gives Wren—and the scattered Aldermen—a home in the free cities.
about_author: Beatrix Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about oaths, borders, and the people who fall between them from a cluttered study full of unlabeled maps.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unspent Words
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She audits the guild's winter ledger, cataloguing impossible trades while suppressing the hum of words rising in her throat. A routine delivery reminds her how carefully invisible she has made herself. Emotional beat: the ache of a gift deliberately buried.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On a salt-stung night, a child scratches at the guild door speaking a language that makes Dominic's oath-bond burn. The child carries an iron key stamped with a sigil Dominic hasn't seen since childhood. Emotional beat: dread and recognition entwined.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She hides the girl among the guild's stockrooms, learning her name and fragments of her story: soldiers burned her village of speakers. The sigil matches one in the guild's oldest, forbidden ledger. Emotional beat: reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Master Quillon's POV. The guildmaster discovers the child and weighs profit against peril, revealing the guild once trafficked in doors between countries. He orders Dominic to appraise the key. Emotional beat: institutional greed masking fear.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the forbidden folios she finds the Door of Aldermere recorded as 'paid in full, sealed by oath.' Her own family name appears as the sealing signatory. Emotional beat: vertigo at discovering her inheritance of betrayal.

chapters.title: Riders on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Sergeant Ilva's POV. The usurper's vanguard reaches the free cities' outskirts, carrying warrants for 'linguists and their harborers.' Ilva, a conscript with doubts, sees a prisoner interrogated for a single word. Emotional beat: creeping complicity.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Quillon offers to sell Wren's location to save the guild. Dominic refuses, burning the relevant page, and is stripped of her rank. Emotional beat: the first cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Found Company
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Dominic flees with Wren, gathering allies: Ferro, a disgraced mapmaker; Sable, a thief who steals memories; and old Nan Hollis, who remembers Alderman lullabies. Emotional beat: the fragile warmth of a forming family.

chapters.title: Maps of Countries That Aren't
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro reveals his life's secret work: reconstructing Aldermere from marginalia, trade routes, and song. His maps show the door lies beneath the free cities themselves. Emotional beat: obsession transfigured into hope.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: Ilva's POV. The usurper publicly declares the free cities harboring 'the last tongue.' Ilva is ordered to lead house-to-house searches and recognizes the hunt is really for a child. Emotional beat: conscience sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: First Word, First Blade
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Ambushed in a fish market, Dominic speaks a word of power for the first time in fifteen years, shattering a squad's weapons—but the effort nearly kills her, and the sound draws every hunter in the city. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of the gift returning.

chapters.title: Nan Hollis Sings
chapters.summary: Nan's POV. Nan teaches Wren songs that are actually maps in disguise; Wren's fluency unlocks verses no adult speaker could parse. They learn the door answers only to a full sentence spoken by two voices. Emotional beat: grief and joy braided in memory.

chapters.title: The Memory Thief's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable offers to steal the location of the door from a captured guild clerk, but each stolen memory costs her a piece of her own past. She takes the risk anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice as love language.

chapters.title: Under the Founders' Stones
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Following Sable's stolen knowledge, the group descends beneath the city's oldest quarter and finds a threshold carved with the Alderman sigil—sealed shut, cold, and watched. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Ilva Turns Her Coat
chapters.summary: Ilva's POV. Ordered to seal the undercity, Ilva falsifies her reports instead and slips warning to Dominic through a bread-seller. Emotional beat: the quiet terror of treason.

chapters.title: Quillon's Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Quillon's POV. The usurper's agents raid the guild; Quillon, protecting his ledgers over his people, is made an example. Dying, he sends Dominic his oldest key and a note: 'Some things were never for sale.' Emotional beat: too-late redemption.

chapters.title: Two Voices
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic and Wren attempt the opening sentence together; the door stirs but demands a true oath renewed, and Dominic cannot yet say the words that bound her family to seal it. Emotional beat: the past as lock.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Free Cities Begins
chapters.summary: Ilva's POV. The usurper's army invests the city walls; refugees flood in, among them other half-speakers drawn by rumor of Wren. Emotional beat: history repeating as pressure mounts.

chapters.title: The Half-Speakers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A dozen broken remnants of Alderman families join them, each carrying a fragment of the language. Together they can assemble the full sentence—but trust must be built across decades of hiding. Emotional beat: scattered pieces finding shape.

chapters.title: What Dominic Forsook
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn why she abandoned her gift: as a girl she spoke a word that killed, and her mother sealed her own memory of it inside Sable's guild. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Envoy
chapters.summary: Envoy Corvane's POV. The usurper's envoy offers Dominic pardon and restoration if she surrenders Wren, revealing the usurper himself is an Alderman exile who wants the door to reclaim a kingdom, not a homeland. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Sable's Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers the memory she needs—of the door's true price—is the one she already sold years ago to buy her freedom. She must steal herself back from the guild vaults. Emotional beat: confronting the self you traded away.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Vault
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A heist into the ruined guild vaults recovers Sable's memory and Quillon's final ledger page: the door was sealed not to imprison Aldermere, but to keep something from following the exiles out. Emotional beat: the plan cracking open.

chapters.title: The Thing Behind the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Through dreams, Wren meets what waits beyond: not a monster, but the country itself, starving, its voice worn down to hunger. It only wants to be remembered—or so it says. Emotional beat: sympathy for the dangerous.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The half-speakers split: some want the door opened for homecoming, others sealed forever. A night argument becomes a knife-drawn standoff until Wren, terrified, runs into the besieged streets. Emotional beat: found family tested.

chapters.title: Wren in the Burning City
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Lost in the bombardment, Wren uses her language openly to shield strangers, and the city begins to whisper of a child who speaks miracles. Ilva finds her and defects fully. Emotional beat: innocence becoming courage.

chapters.title: Corvane's Trap
chapters.summary: Ilva's POV. Ilva delivers Wren to Corvane as a double agent, buying time—but Corvane suspects, and the usurper's own half-speakers begin translating the door's sentence from stolen fragments. Emotional beat: a gamble balanced on a blade.

chapters.title: The Sentence Assembled
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Combining Wren's fluency, Nan's songs, Ferro's maps, and the half-speakers' fragments, they complete the opening sentence—and understand its final clause requires a willing oath-breaker to stand in the doorway. Emotional beat: destiny narrowing to a single choice.

chapters.title: Oath-Bound Again
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic formally renews the swordspeaker's oath before the assembled half-speakers—not to seal or open, but to guard whatever comes through. Her burned-out gift flares back to life. Emotional beat: reclaiming identity without shame.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Quiet interlude: mended clothes, shared meals, confessions. Nan dies peacefully after teaching Wren the last verse, asking to be buried facing Aldermere. Emotional beat: tenderness before the storm.

chapters.title: Breach at the Founders' Stones
chapters.summary: Ilva's POV. The usurper's forces break into the undercity; Ilva holds the stair with a handful of defectors. Ferro collapses a tunnel to slow them, sealing himself on the wrong side. Emotional beat: valor and loss.

chapters.title: The Door Stands Open
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The sentence spoken, the Door of Aldermere grinds open onto a grey, wind-scoured country—and something vast begins to pour its attention through. Dominic takes her place in the threshold. Emotional beat: terrible wonder.

chapters.title: The Usurper Arrives
chapters.summary: Usurper Aldous's POV. The usurper himself descends, revealing he was the boy who fled Aldermere first and left everyone else to burn. He demands the door for conquest; Dominic refuses him passage. Emotional beat: mirror-match of two exiles.

chapters.title: Words as Blades
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Duel of languages: Aldous wields the tongue as domination, Dominic as shelter. Wren joins voices with her, and together they unmake Aldous's stolen words, leaving him mute and mortal. Emotional beat: power answered by belonging.

chapters.title: The Holding
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. To keep the door from devouring or being devoured, Dominic pours her restored gift into the threshold, becoming its living hinge—present but unable to leave. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, grief and peace together.

chapters.title: What Came Through
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. What emerges is not an army but seeds, songs, and the country's memory offered freely now that it is witnessed rather than imprisoned. The half-speakers begin planting Aldermere in free-city soil. Emotional beat: mourning turning to rootedness.

chapters.title: The Ledger of New Things
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable opens a new guild trading in returned memories and Alderman crafts, keeping Dominic's ledger going at the door, reading entries aloud to her daily. Emotional beat: devotion as continuity.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Revised
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Spring: Alderman festivals braid into free-city streets; Ilva trains a watch that guards rather than hunts; Wren teaches children the language as a living thing, not a weapon. Emotional beat: belonging earned and shared.

chapters.title: The Thorn Turns Again
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the threshold, Wren tells Dominic the old proverb that names the book: a thorn that turns becomes a rose's root. Dominic, the door's keeper, smiles for the first time in the story. Emotional beat: transformation acknowledged.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Sentence
chapters.summary: Dominic and Wren, alternating. Years later, Wren stands at the door as a grown speaker, and the two complete the closing sentence together—not sealing it, but blessing it, so it opens only for the homesick. Emotional beat: the arc completed; family as the door that never shuts.
